summary.text: Sara Love is a Democratic member of the Maryland State Senate from District 16 who was appointed in June 2024 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney and former public policy director for the ACLU of Maryland, she previously served in the House of Delegates.

paragraphs.text: Love was born in Evanston, Illinois, on April 6, 1967, and earned a bachelor's degree in American history from Princeton University in 1989 and a law degree from Northwestern University School of Law in 1992.

She clerked for Judge Timothy K. Lewis of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, was a litigation associate in Chicago, and was general counsel of the National Women's Health Foundation from 1998 to 2004.
She was public policy director of ACLU of Maryland from 2012 to 2016 and served on its board, including as president from 2008 to 2012.
Love served in the House of Delegates from 2019 to 2024 on the Environment and Transportation Committee, chairing its Motor Vehicle and Transportation Subcommittee in 2023 and 2024.
Gov. Wes Moore appointed her to the Senate in June 2024 to replace Sen. Ariana Kelly, and she has been a member since June 13, 2024.
She serves on the Judicial Proceedings Committee, is vice chair of the Montgomery County Senate Delegation, and sits on the Chesapeake Bay Commission.
She advanced from the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026.
